commits.message: test: the hang detector's comment names the budgets that really differ (rich-test-suite-umkj)

test: the hang detector covers hooks too, and names what keeps its own budget (rich-test-suite-umkj)

Review of #281: hookTimeout stayed at vitest's 10s, so the first hook that
spawns under load would restart the per-file chase. Both timeouts now read
one constant. The comment no longer claims only speed tests set a budget;
the vite-build tests' 60s is work longer by nature.

test: one 30s hang detector for the whole suite, not per file (rich-test-suite-umkj)

Tests that spawn git, npm, node or a vite build cross vitest's 5s default
under a full suite's load, and per-describe allowances only ever covered the
file that had last flaked. vitest.config.ts now sets testTimeout once; the
eight 30s describe overrides that copied it are gone. Budgets that differ
(the 2s termination guards, the 60s-180s builds) stay beside their tests.

Three concurrent full suites, three times: 9 of 9 runs failed on a 5s
timeout before (ascii-only), 9 of 9 green after. A never-resolving test
still fails, at 30s.

test(docs): the simulated-process suite allows a vite build's time under load (rich-tests-lazu) (#280)

Most runInTerminal cases vite-build the library before running it; under a
full suite's load the overlapping-runs case crossed vitest's 5s default
(3 of ~9 full runs on 2026-09-29). The describe now carries the 30s
allowance example-runner and playground-program already give their builds.
6 of 6 full npm test runs green after.
